OD1.currentOperation: STBY waiting for BOUM-0001 location clearance, to start jack-down and move to BM-0001
OD1.nextSteps: Rig preparation for move; rig move for new well BOUM-0001

highlights: OD1 stayed on standby for BOUM-0001 location clearance, now to start jack-down and move to BM-0001. Last week activities are recorded as Nil: the rig was idle for the full seven days.
Overstay crew rose from 10 to 11, all of them COSL. KOC and HLB are nil.
OD1 personnel onboard rose from 75 to 79. 57 of the 79 hold a seaman or business visa.
Ground transport turned sharply inbound: 32 arrivals against 12 dispatches, 44 moves in total against 41. The week before ran 35 out and 6 in, so the direction reversed.

The inbound load is the BM-0001 move materials: 18-5/8" and 24" casing and short joints, a casing spool, X-overs, and Fugro positioning tools, from KOC Ahmadi Yard-4 and Yard-5 and HETCO Mina Abdallah. Arrivals peaked on Wed 09 Sep with 9.
Fluids handled more than doubled, 1,782 m³ against 742 m³. Fuel delivered to the rigs rose from 200 m³ to 394 m³, of which CA1 transferred 260 m³ on Sun 06 Sep.
Vessel trips rose to 13 from 9, per the covering email: CA1 6, CA3 2, CA5 nil, Charlie-3 5. CA1 carried the increase, working OD1 and OPH through the week. See the data queries on the counting basis.
OPH stayed off-hired for a third week, and still drew cargo and fluids: CA1 delivered 300 m³ of fresh water and 294 m³ of fuel to OPH across 03 and 07 Sep.
Port status reads Normal on all 7 days, where both previous weeks read Not Normal on every day. The port again ran day shift only.
dataNotes: Trips are taken from the covering email (13), which supersedes the workbook. Settled 10 Sep. The workbook narrative yields 8 on the rule used for the two earlier weeks, one outbound voyage from Shuaiba plus its return; the difference is 4 further rig calls by CA1 and 1 by CA3, so the email appears to count rig calls rather than port voyages. For the two earlier weeks the email and the workbook agree exactly, so the 13 against 9 rise may reflect the change of basis as well as activity. Worth confirming once with the author so later weeks stay comparable.

Vessel sheet 06.09: CA1 is recorded STBY at OPH, but on 05.09 it was approaching OD1 at 23:48 and on 07.09 it heaved up at OPH. One of the two rig names is likely wrong, which also affects where the 260.2 m³ of fuel went.
Vessel sheet 09.09: Charlie-3 casts off at 11:25 and is alongside OPH at 11:30. That transit is not possible in five minutes.
The well is named BOUM-0001, BM-0001 and BM-001 across the email and the workbook. Confirm the correct designation.

Port sheet 07.09 rows E30 and E33 are word for word identical, same call-off OD-BM1-A-1-4. They are counted as two trucks because E35 records two trucks with chemical containers offloaded, which confirms two.

The Port sheet records bunkering less precisely than the Vessel sheet. Port E10 gives fresh water 216 m³ to CA3, where Vessel E5 splits the same delivery into fresh water 144 m³ and drilling water 72 m³. The Vessel sheet is used. The Port sheet also has no bunkering line for 05.09, where Vessel E12 records 108 m³ to CA1.
Fuel volumes are recorded to three decimals (35.997, 107.999, 71.99) and are read as 36, 108 and 72 m³.

Offload lines repeat arrivals already counted: E21 repeats E19, E23 repeats E24 to E27, E34 and E35 repeat E30 to E33, and E49 and E50 repeat E42, E43 and E46. Each truck is counted once, on arrival. Counting the offloads as well would add 14 movements.
Reporting window is 7 days (03 to 09 Sep) against 8 days for the previous report, so absolute counts are not like for like. The comparison table carries a per day row.
